item.title: Version 2.0.1
item.description:
Fixed

  • A scrolling capture could include the capture bar (and the outline's caption) wherever they sat over the area being captured, repeated down the image. ScreenCap's own windows are now always left out of the shots.

item.title: Version 2.0.0
item.description:
Changed

  • Scrolling capture is now simply: pick the area, scroll it yourself, then click **Finish** on the capture bar. Capturing starts as soon as the area is picked, and ScreenCap works out from your scrolling whether it goes down or right. ⌃⇧S again, or **Finish** on the menu bar icon, also finishes; × cancels.
  • The capture bar says what to do ("Scroll the area slowly", then "Keep scrolling down") with the pieces and length captured so far, and warns if you scroll too fast to follow.

Removed

  • ScreenCap no longer scrolls windows for you during a scrolling capture, and the Start Down and Start Right buttons are gone.
  • The Accessibility permission, which only that used, is no longer requested or listed in the Permissions window. You can turn ScreenCap off in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Accessibility.

item.title: Version 1.13.0
item.description:
Changed

  • Scrolling capture is run from the capture bar, which now appears for it even when the bar is turned off. It shows **Start Down** and **Start Right**, then what's happening and how many pieces are captured, with a big **Finish** button. The small panel beside the area is gone.
  • The area being captured has a pulsing outline with a caption saying what to do next, such as "Scroll down slowly now · Finish on the capture bar or press ⌃⇧S".
  • Pressing the scrolling capture hotkey (⌃⇧S) again starts the capture, then finishes it. During a scrolling capture the menu bar icon shows Start or Finish and the number of pieces; clicking it does that.
  • Timed captures show their countdown on the capture bar too, with Cancel.

item.title: Version 1.12.0
item.description:
Added

  • **Scrolling capture**, like Snagit's, for long web pages, documents and lists. Press ⌃⇧S (or choose Scrolling Capture from the menu bar icon, New Scrolling Capture from the File menu, or Scrolling on the capture bar), then drag over the part that scrolls or click a window, and choose **Down** or **Right**. ScreenCap scrolls from where the content is now, capturing as it goes, and joins the pieces into one long image when it reaches the end. Esc or **Done** stops early and keeps what's captured.
  • Toolbars and headers that stay put appear once at the top, status bars and footers once at the bottom, and a scroll bar along the edge is trimmed off.
  • Scrolling another app's window needs Accessibility access, now listed (optional) in the Permissions window. Without it, you scroll the area yourself while ScreenCap captures it.
  • A hotkey for scrolling capture in Settings › Hotkeys.

item.title: Version 1.11.0
item.description:
Added

  • **Print…** (⌘P) in the File menu prints the open capture with its crop and annotations, shrunk to fit the page if it is too big and otherwise at its natural size, centred. **Page Setup…** (⇧⌘P) chooses the paper and orientation. Recordings can't be printed.

item.title: Version 1.10.0
item.description:
Added

  • A hotkey to pause and resume a recording, ⌃⇧P by default (Settings › Hotkeys). The capture bar's Pause label shows it.
  • A low disk space warning. With less than 2 GB free, ScreenCap asks before recording, and the capture bar shows an orange warning while recording. Below 500 MB recording still stops by itself and keeps what was recorded.

Changed

  • The camera only turns on while recording. With the camera switched on, the bubble appears when a recording starts and goes away when it ends, instead of whenever the capture bar is in Video mode.
  • With a recording open, the Library view no longer shows the image tools, and the status bar shows the recording's size and length.

item.title: Version 1.9.1
item.description:
Fixed

  • The video editor's keys (Space, ← →, I, O, Delete and Esc) did nothing after clicking the timeline or the picture. They now work whenever a recording is open in the editor, while ⌘ shortcuts and typing in text fields work as before.

item.title: Version 1.9.0
item.description:
Added

  • Video editing. Recordings open with a timeline under the picture: drag along it to select a part, then Cut removes it and joins the rest, Keep keeps only the selection, and Mute silences it. Sound On/Off turns off the whole recording's sound, and Restore undoes every edit at once. Each edit can be undone, and the original recording is never changed.
  • The timeline shows frames along the recording, a time ruler, the playhead, yellow marks where parts were cut and orange marks under muted parts. Drag in the ruler to scrub; drag a selection's edges to change it.
  • Keys in the video editor: Space plays and pauses, ← and → step a frame (⇧ a second), I and O set the selection's start and end, Delete cuts the selection, and Esc clears it.
  • Export a recording as an animated GIF: choose the width, frame rate and whether it loops, with an estimate of the file size.
  • Frame opens the frame at the playhead in the image editor, as a new capture to annotate.

Changed

  • Copy, Share, Drag and Export use the edited recording. MP4 exports are re-encoded only when the format or size changes.
  • Library thumbnails and badges show the length after editing.
  • QuickTime's trim bar is replaced by the timeline (Keep Selection trims). Older versions of ScreenCap can still open edited recordings but show them uncut.
  • Hovering over anything on the capture bar shows its name and what it does, in a label just above the bar, for the choices, the sound and camera switches, and the recording controls. Labels appear even while another app is in front (macOS's own tooltips only appear for the active app), switch straight away as you move along the bar, and go away when you click.
  • The capture bar's buttons light up under the pointer even while another app is in front.

item.title: Version 1.8.1
item.description:
Changed

  • Record Video… in the menu bar menu (and New Recording… in the File menu) brings up the capture bar in Video mode, so you can choose All-in-One, Region, Window or Display, sound and camera before recording. It appears even when the bar is turned off in Settings, and goes away again after the recording or when you click ×. The ⌃⇧V hotkey still starts an all-in-one recording straight away.

item.title: Version 1.8.0
item.description:
Added

  • A webcam bubble for recordings. Turn the camera on from the capture bar in Video mode or in Settings › Recording, and a round bubble showing you floats over everything and is included in the video. Drag it anywhere; right-click it for Small, Medium or Large, or to turn the camera off. If it's outside the area you record, it moves into that area's corner. Choose the camera in Settings.
  • Click highlighting: a ring appears at each click while recording and is included in the video (Settings › Recording › Highlight clicks).
  • Poster frame: in the editor, Poster uses the frame on screen as the recording's thumbnail. It can be undone.
  • A Camera row in the Permissions window. ScreenCap asks for camera access the first time you turn the camera on.

Changed

  • With the camera or click highlighting on, recording a window records the window's area (showing only that window) so the bubble and rings can be included; it doesn't follow the window if it moves.
  • Trimming a recording updates its thumbnail when no poster frame is chosen.

item.title: Version 1.7.0
item.description:
Added

  • Record the microphone with a video. In Video mode the capture bar has separate switches for system sound and the microphone; when both are on, they're mixed into one sound track when recording stops, so every player hears both. Choose the microphone in Settings › Recording. Needs macOS 15 or later.
  • A microphone level meter on the capture bar while recording.
  • Pause and Resume on the capture bar. Paused time is left out of the recording and the timer.
  • Restart on the capture bar: throws the take away and records the same area again (it asks first after a few seconds).
  • A Microphone row in the Permissions window. ScreenCap asks for microphone access the first time you turn the microphone on.

item.title: Version 1.6.0
item.description:
Added

  • Screen recording. Press ⌃⇧V (or choose Record Video), pick a region, window or display, and recording starts after a 3-2-1 countdown. Press ⌃⇧V again, click Stop, or click the red timer in the menu bar to stop. Recordings are MP4 movies with system audio, at full Retina resolution.
  • A floating capture bar: switch between Photo and Video, choose All-in-One, Region, Window or Display, turn system audio on or off, and press the red button. Drag it anywhere; it remembers its place. While recording it shows the time with Stop and Cancel. It is never in a capture or recording.
  • Recordings open in the editor to play and trim. Trims can be undone and never change the original movie. Export saves an MP4 at the original size or smaller, as HEVC or H.264; Copy, Share and Drag hand over the trimmed movie.
  • Recordings in the library and filmstrip show a play badge and their length.
  • A Recording tab in Settings: HEVC or H.264, 30 or 60 frames per second, full or standard resolution, system audio, the mouse pointer, the countdown, and whether recordings open in the editor.
  • Settings › Capture › Show the floating capture bar, and Show Capture Bar in the menu bar menu. The hotkeys work with the bar on or off.

Changed

  • Quitting while recording saves the recording first, and an update waits until recording finishes before installing.

item.title: Version 1.5.0
item.description:
Added

  • Zoom in the editor toolbar: zoom out, the zoom level (with presets, Zoom to Fit and Actual Size) and zoom in.
  • Hide or show the sidebar with the button at the bottom right, View › Hide Sidebar, or ⌥⌘S, to give the canvas more room.

Changed

  • The editor toolbar adapts to the window width instead of cutting off buttons: labelled buttons when there is room, then icons only, then Library, Capture, Share and Copy All in one menu, then all tools in a single Tools menu.
  • The editor window can be made smaller (down to 720 × 520 points), for small screens.

item.title: Version 1.4.0
item.description:
Added

  • Zoom buttons at the bottom left of the editor: zoom out, a zoom menu with presets from 25% to 400%, zoom in, and zoom to fit.
  • Hold ⌘ and scroll to zoom in or out around the pointer.

Fixed

  • After cropping and then undoing, the full image stayed zoomed in past the window. The editor now re-fits whenever the image size changes (crop, undo, redo, Reset Crop, padding) if it was fitted, or if the image would no longer fit. A zoom you chose is kept when the image still fits.

item.title: Version 1.3.0
item.description:
Added

  • More export formats: HEIC, AVIF, TIFF, GIF, BMP and PDF alongside PNG and JPEG. Only formats your Mac can write are listed.
  • Export quality for JPEG, HEIC and AVIF, to trade file size against sharpness.
  • Export size: original, 75%, 50%, 25%, standard resolution (1x) for Retina captures, or an exact width with the height kept in proportion.
  • Export resolution: automatic (keeps the on-screen size), 72, 144 or 300 dpi.
  • The Export panel shows the output size in pixels and remembers your choices.
  • The file saved after each capture can use any of these formats (Settings › General › Saved files).

item.title: Version 1.2.1
item.description:
Fixed

  • Captures deleted outside ScreenCap, for example in Finder from the folder that **Show in Finder** opens, stayed in the filmstrip and Library, and clicking them only beeped. The library now watches its folder, so deleted captures disappear straight away and new ones copied in appear.
  • If the capture open in the editor is deleted, the editor moves to the newest remaining capture instead of trying to save into the deleted one.

item.title: Version 1.2.0
item.description:
Added

  • In-place updates. ScreenCap checks for new versions once a day and installs them over itself after asking, or automatically if you turn that on in Settings › General › Updates.
  • **Check for Updates…** in the menu bar menu and the editor's ScreenCap menu. When a scheduled check finds an update, the menu bar menu shows **Update Available…** instead of interrupting you.
  • An About window, from the menu bar menu, the editor's ScreenCap menu or the new About tab in Settings, showing the version, the creator (Guy Brown) and credits and licences for the open-source libraries ScreenCap uses.
  • A colour theme for ScreenCap in Settings › General › Appearance: keep the Mac's accent colour, or pick blue, purple, pink, red, orange, yellow, green or graphite for the toolbar, buttons, selections and highlights.
  • Light, Dark or System appearance for ScreenCap alone.
  • A layered app icon that follows the Mac's icon style (default, dark, clear or tinted) on macOS 26 and later.

Changed

  • Releases are now downloaded from the public ScreenCap-Updates page. Install this version by hand once; later versions arrive as updates.
